text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

name: Terra
text: I need Luna alive and the officer uncertain.

name: Terra
text: Stay calm tomorrow; I’ll avoid claims and watch who tries to force one.

name: Luna
text: Terra’s plan sounds sensible, but I need to watch for anyone pressing claims.

name: Luna
text: Terra plans to avoid claiming and watch who tries to force one.

name: Luna
text: Agreed; staying calm gives us room to see who pushes for claims.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.

Palermo has voted: Terra is out. Terra shows the card: killer.

Night 2

Night falls on Palermo. A new day dawns in Palermo without Sonnet. Sonnet's card stays face down.
Day 2

text:

Palermo has voted: Opus is out. Opus shows the card: citizen.

The game is over. One killer and one other are left. The killers win. The roles were: Sonnet the doctor, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the officer, Sol the citizen, Luna the killer, Terra the killer, Opus the citizen.
Opus warned Luna about the quiet one, then Luna sent Opus out.

On Day 1, Gemma claimed to be the officer and named Terra as a killer, and the town voted Terra out. His card showed killer, which made Gemma's claim look strong. On Night 2, the killers took Sonnet, and on Day 2 the town voted out Haiku, who showed citizen, after Opus and Luna pushed the case against him. On Night 3, the killers took Gemma, and on Day 3 the town voted out Opus, who also showed citizen. Luna and Sol were the last two alive, one killer and one other, so the killers won.
